text:
alex: noticed a regression in tail-latency on the kv-prefetch workload after the batching heuristic tweak yesterday

mira: saw it too, only on multi-gpu nodes with NVLink enabled :thinking_face:

jon: quick summary: overall throughput stable, p99 jumps from ~120ms -> ~220ms for some small sequences when cache misses happen

alex: exact symptom is H2D stalls and long peercopy queuing in nsys timeline, NVLink shows repeated tiny bursts, then a big stall

yao: can you paste the nsys capture? any perf counters?

alex: attaching snippet from the capture (trimmed) -- command we ran:
```
nsys profile -o kvpref-nvlink -t cuda,osrt,kernel -f true --sample=none --wait=10 --capture-range=host:thread:0-1000 --trace-cuda-activities=true 
./run_kv_prefetch --model=gptx --batch=8 --seq=1024
```

alex: timeline excerpt:
```
GPU0 H2D memcpy 0.12ms
GPU0 Kernel A (kv_lookup) 1.8ms
GPU0 PeerCopy GPU1->GPU0 0.06ms
... repeated peercopy bursts ...
GPU0 PeerCopy queued 14.2ms (waiting on stream 7)
GPU0 Kernel B (decoder) 3.4ms    <-- gets serialized after big wait
```

mira: interesting that peercopy queued time is where CPU side is idle, suggests stream contention on the receiving GPU or unexpected mechanical serialization

jon: I also see that the kernel selection changed: small-batch path used fp16-fused-kernel yesterday, but after the heuristic tweak it sometimes picks the fallback generic kernel which does more host-syncs

alex: yep, kernel switch + increase in prefetch count -> more small H2D transfers instead of aggregated transfer -> PCIe/NVLink oversubscription

yao: did we switch memory allocation to pageable for prefetch buffer? that would force staging copies and cause pageable stalls

alex: we did for one optimization: changed allocator to use default cudaMalloc instead of cudaMallocHost for prefetch arena to reduce fragmentation. suspect that's part of it

mira: quick check: `cudaMemcpyAsync` from pageable will do implicit staging and can block on H2D path. that pairs poorly with many small transfers across NVLink

jon: pasted perf counters from capture:
```
SM active: 78%
NVLINK tx bytes: 4.2GB
PCIe tx bytes: 1.9GB
H2D memcpy stalls (pageable): 12k cycles spike around misses
```

alex: so hypothesis: batching heuristic increases prefetch count -> more small reads -> allocator uses pageable -> lots of small H2D through staging -> peercopy stream queuing on receive -> kernel fallback and serialization -> p99 spikes

mira: what about kernel timeline ordering? maybe async streams ordering changed too after heuristic: prefetch runs on stream 3, model kernels on stream 0, peer copies on stream 1, and we rely on implicit stream syncs

yao: if peer copies use default stream on the receiving GPU they might create synchronization points that serialize kernels. need to confirm stream indices in the trace

alex: here's the trace filter I used to extract stream activity:
```
nsys nvlink --list-streams kvpref-nvlink.qdrep | egrep "H2D|D2H|Memcpy|PeerCopy|Kernel"
```

jon: next steps I propose:
- switch allocator back to pinned (cudaMallocHost) for prefetch arena and re-run
- force batching heuristic to cap prefetches per request to 4 (was 12)
- capture perfetto for cross-check and enable `cudaMemcpyKind` annotations if possible

mira: +1. also add a run that forces peercopy to fallback to PCIe (set env NVLINK_DISABLE=1) to compare queuing behavior

yao: I'll run three traces: (1) current master, (2) pinned allocator + capped prefetch, (3) NVLINK_DISABLE=1. I'll drop the qdrep and upload tar.gz

ci-bot: build #4821 succeeded for branch perf/kv-prefetch-heuristic. Artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/perf/kvpref/4821

alex: thanks, @yao. when you have traces, post links. if pinned + cap fixes p99 we can make a small revert for allocator and add a followup optimization that aggregates small transfers into a single batched H2D per request

jon: also worth adding a test to the perf harness that runs under NVLink-enabled instances and asserts p99 < 150ms for that workload to catch regressions early

mira: noted. I'll add an e2e check in the CI perf suite (lightweight, sample size 64).

yao: started run 1 (master) 1932109886, run 2 queued, will post links in ~8m

alex: one more thing — watch for unusual kernel names in nsys: if you see `generic_mm_kern` or `memcopy_staging` that's a red flag for fallback paths

mira: good call. also check for repeated cudaStreamSynchronize calls on hot paths (shows up as host-side gaps in timeline)

jon: thanks all. if this is confirmed I'll open a small PR to revert the allocator change and cap prefetches until we design a proper aggregated transfer approach

alex: perfect. keep it light on changes until we validate. :white_check_mark:

yao: uploading master trace: https://s3.redwood.ai/perf/kvpref/master_1932109886_qdrep.tar.gz

mira: got it, downloading now

ci-bot: trace artifact scanned and available (sha256: b8f3c6...)

alex: leaving notes here for anyone picking this up: - look for `PeerCopy queued` durations, - check for pageable staging markers, - correlate kernel selection logs from runtime with nsys timeline

jon: tagging this thread `perf-regression` and `nvlink` for search.

mira: will update after runs complete.

yao: run 2 (pinned + cap) uploaded: https://s3.redwood.ai/perf/kvpref/pinned_cap_1932109896_qdrep.tar.gz

alex: preliminary look: pinned+cap reduced PeerCopy queued time from median 8ms -> 0.3ms and p99 dropped to ~140ms. promising.

mira: awesome. let's draft the revert PR and add the aggregation task to the backlog.

jon: I'll draft the PR later today. closing loop here. :rocket:
